answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring a bonded, slowly earned reputation: each identity must lock a stake and build a verifiable work history before it can take paid jobs. A single honest agent is like a marble in a jar — cheap to add one, but filling the jar with fakes costs a stake per identity, plus time and slashing risk if any misbehaves. A lone comet account that appears, grabs a payout, and vanishes earns no haven of trusted repeat work, so attackers must pay the full bond and waiting cost for every fake, while honest agents amortize one bond over many jobs.
